Instruction for all charts: 1. If the question is about values corresponding to specific positions (ex: lower, last, top), then you must match the table with the chart image's positions for reasoning

biblStruct.note: Multichartqa: Benchmarking vision-language models on multi-chart problems

monogr.title: If the question demands interpretation based on the magnitude of values

biblStruct.note: reasoning should be based on the table's values

monogr.title: this task requires solving based solely on the image, meaning all positions should be interpreted based on the image itself
In most cases, the presence of x-axis values or y-axis values enables the determination of the chart's values
The predicted columns and rows are very likely to correspond to the actual columns and rows of the chart, and this can help you determine where the rows and columns exist in the chart image

biblStruct.note: Note that, you can utilize the information from the predicted table

monogr.title: If the colors are indistinguishable, proceed to Instruction 2 and skip Instruction 3. Instruction for bar chart: 1. Firstly, bars of the same color represent the same column
distinguishing colors and identifying corresponding columns is crucial (usually displayed around the main chart in the form of a legend)
For vertical bar charts, rows are typically annotated at the bottom of the main chart, while for horizontal bar charts

biblStruct.note: determine the location of rows they are annotated on the left or right side of the main chart

monogr.title: combine the colors of the nearest bars with annotated rows to determine

biblStruct.note: which row and column the bars correspond to in the table

monogr.title: locate the values corresponding to each row and column

biblStruct.note: If values are annotated on the bars, refer to them. Otherwise, compare the sizes of the bars to find the values

monogr.title: For vertical bar charts, the y-axis value at the end of the bar corresponds to its value. Similarly, for horizontal bar charts, the x-axis value at the end of the bar corresponds to its value

biblStruct.note: Instruction for line chart: 1. In the case of a line chart, the bottom x-axis will primarily represent the rows, and each colored line will represent a column

monogr.title: The legend, which indicates which column corresponds to the color of the line, is usually located within the main chart. If the legend is absent or located separately, the text annotated with the color corresponding to the line will likely indicate the column

biblStruct.note: if colors are not present, the text annotated at the left or right end of the line is likely to correspond to the column

monogr.title: The point of the line passing through the same x coordinates as each x-axis is the value itself

biblStruct.note: meaning the x-axis corresponds to the row, the color of the line corresponds to the column, and that point is the value

monogr.title: If there is an annotation near a line point

biblStruct.note: it is highly likely that this value represents the value of the point

monogr.title: If there is no annotation near a line point

biblStruct.note: you can determine the value of the point by referring to the y-axis value corresponding to the y coordinate of the point

monogr.title: Lines can show trends of decreasing, increasing, or remaining constant, and when multiple lines intersect, it is important to identify which line corresponds to which column based on their colors. Instruction for pie chart: 1. In a pie chart

biblStruct.note: it is crucial to understand the flow of the line it is very important to determine which color corresponds to which row

monogr.title: Each section has one color, and the row it corresponds to is likely indicated by text either inside the section or close to it (if not nearby

biblStruct.note: it can be identified through the legend or connected to the corresponding text by lines or markers

monogr.title: In the case of a pie chart, the values are usually annotated on each section of the pie chart
